title.my: အခြေခံ သဒ္ဒါ

rule.en:
Have / has: I, you, we, they have. He, she, it has. I have a brother. / She has a laptop.

Possessive adjectives: my, your, his, her, its, our, their come before a noun. This is my bag. / That is her desk. We do not say This is me bag.

Singular/plural nouns: one book → two books, one child → two children. Before a singular countable noun, use an article or another determiner: I have a sister. Not I have sister.

Be vs have: She is a teacher. (identity); She has a laptop. (possession). Do not say She is a laptop. to mean ownership.
rule.my: ပိုင်ဆိုင်မှုကို ပြောသည့်အခါ have/has ကို သုံးပါ။ I/you/we/they နှင့် have၊ he/she/it နှင့် has ကို တွဲသုံးသည်။ My/your/his/her/its/our/their သည် ပိုင်ရှင်ကို ညွှန်းပြီး နာမ်ရှေ့၌ ရှိသည် — my phone၊ her book။ Its သည် it ၏ ပိုင်ဆိုင်မှုညွှန်းစကား ဖြစ်ပြီး it's (it is) နှင့် မတူပါ။ Is သည် လူတစ်ယောက် ဘယ်သူဖြစ်သည်၊ ဘယ်လိုဖြစ်သည်ကို ဖော်ပြ၍ has သည် ပိုင်ဆိုင်မှုကို ဖော်ပြသည်။ အနည်းကိန်း ရေတွက်နိုင်သော နာမ်ရှေ့တွင် a/an သို့မဟုတ် အခြားအညွှန်းစကား လိုသည်။ Book ၏ အများကိန်းမှာ books၊ child ၏ အများကိန်းမှာ children ဖြစ်သည်။

ကျွန်ုပ်တွင် ကလေး နှစ်ယောက် ရှိသည်။

body.en:
My sister has a phone. / Incorrect: My sister have a phone.
This is his bag. / Incorrect: This is he bag.
They are my friends. / Incorrect: They is my friends.
I have two children. / Incorrect: I have two childs.

rule.en:
Present simple for habits: I start work at ten. / She starts work at nine. Add -s or -es with he/she/it in affirmative clauses: He watches TV.

Negative: I do not (don't) work on Sunday. / She does not (doesn't) work on Sunday. After doesn't, use the base form: doesn't work, not doesn't works.

Question: Do you work from home? / Does she work from home? Answers: Yes, I do. / No, she doesn't.

Time: at 8:30, on Monday, in the morning, every day. Usually, often, sometimes, and never commonly go before a main verb: I usually study at night. With be: She is usually early.
